Attendees were Emil Muller, Keira Silva, and Scout.

The team reviewed the usual flow for passengers moving through Aurelia Skyways and agreed the desk works best when the welcome team keeps the language simple, warm, and steady. The main point was to make sure pet owners get clear guidance before boarding, with special care for carriers, documents, and calm handoff steps. Everyone agreed that comfort matters just as much as speed, because a nervous traveler often takes their cue from the desk and the crew.

The group talked through common issues from the last round of departures, especially cases where people arrive with mixed paperwork or unclear expectations about pet placement. The desk should keep giving practical instructions early, then repeat them in plain language so no one has to guess. It was also noted that a friendly check-in can prevent later confusion at the skyport, which helps the crew and keeps the passenger experience smoother.

Scout was mentioned during the discussion as a reminder that pets notice tone and routine. The team wants the desk to stay patient, avoid rushed handoffs, and keep the customer first when lines build up. Emil Muller and Keira Silva both supported the idea of a short, consistent script that covers the basics without sounding stiff. The group also agreed to share any repeating concerns with the wider operation so guidance stays current and useful.

The meeting ended after everyone confirmed the next set of desk priorities and the plan for keeping companion animal travel clear, calm, and kind.
